q: A 68-year-old man reports six months of erectile dysfunction. He has no known cardiovascular disease but experiences intermittent chest discomfort with exertion, which he attributes to aging. He takes metformin for type 2 diabetes diagnosed three years ago. Blood pressure is 145/92 mmHg and BMI is 32. Which evaluation addresses the concern raised by this combination before proceeding with erectile-dysfunction treatment?
o: Prescribe sildenafil and arrange follow-up in three months.
Evaluate cardiovascular disease, including stress testing for suspected coronary disease.
Request penile duplex ultrasonography through a urology referral.
Measure morning testosterone and thyroid function as the initial work-up.
explanation:
Erectile dysfunction may be an early manifestation of vascular disease. Exertional chest discomfort and multiple risk factors warrant **cardiovascular evaluation before ED treatment**, including ischemia testing when appropriate.

**A. Prescribe sildenafil and arrange follow-up in three months.** Starting sildenafil immediately postpones the assessment of possible coronary disease and eligibility for sexual activity.
**B. Evaluate cardiovascular disease, including stress testing for suspected coronary disease.** The symptom pattern raises concern for exertional ischemia, which changes management and drug safety.
**C. Request penile duplex ultrasonography through a urology referral.** Penile vascular imaging cannot assess the cause or risk of exertional chest pain.
**D. Measure morning testosterone and thyroid function as the initial work-up.** Hormonal tests can help investigate ED but do not address possible coronary ischemia.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 550, 1567.
ref: Hazzard Ch 37 — SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN
chapterTitle: SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN

q: An older woman with cancer and good ECOG performance status reports falls and forgetfulness. What does comprehensive geriatric assessment add?
o: An assessment that reduces the need to investigate falls when ECOG status is good
An assessment that concentrates on the tumor in place of function and cognition
An assessment that identifies aging-related problems missed by ECOG performance status
An assessment that postpones cognitive evaluation until ECOG performance status deteriorates
explanation:
ECOG performance status summarizes general activity, but a good score can coexist with fall risk or cognitive decline. **Comprehensive geriatric assessment detects problems ECOG can miss**.

**A. Forego falls assessment.** Recurrent falls remain important even in an independent ambulatory patient.
**B. Concentrate on the tumor.** The added information comes from examining patient function, cognition and support.
**C. Look for hidden vulnerabilities.** A falls history and cognitive assessment can uncover actionable problems behind a favorable performance score.
**D. Delay cognitive testing.** Forgetfulness warrants evaluation before a treatment plan relies on her ability to follow it.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1388.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: A 77-year-old man with diabetes and stage 3a chronic kidney disease is hospitalized for pneumonia. On the third day he develops new confusion, difficulty following commands and picking at the sheets; his wife reports that he was cognitively clear the day before. Medications include metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, ceftriaxone and as-needed diphenhydramine for sleep. Which approach fits the medication component of delirium management?
o: Stop diphenhydramine and reassess the confusion
Continue the antihistamine and add routine daytime sedation
Increase the antihistamine to improve the disrupted sleep
Retain the antihistamine while deferring medication review
explanation:
First-generation antihistamines block central muscarinic signaling and can impair attention. As-needed drugs for sleep belong in the medication history.
**Stop the nonessential diphenhydramine and reassess cognition while treating his pneumonia.**

**A. Stop diphenhydramine and reassess the confusion.** Removing the anticholinergic exposure may help and allows the team to observe the clinical course.
**B. Continue the antihistamine and add routine daytime sedation.** Adding daytime sedation increases cognitive burden without addressing the antihistamine.
**C. Increase the antihistamine to improve the disrupted sleep.** More diphenhydramine increases the very exposure that may have precipitated confusion.
**D. Retain the antihistamine while deferring medication review.** Reviewing only scheduled medicines would miss an important, reversible exposure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882–883, 885, Table 58-2

q: An 83-year-old man with heart failure, stage 3b CKD (eGFR 35), and mild dementia is receiving hospice care for end-stage heart disease. Severe peripheral edema is causing skin breakdown and discomfort. He takes morphine 5 mg every four hours and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. His wife asks whether a diuretic could help. Which approach follows the source treatment of symptomatic congestion?
o: Start furosemide with monitoring and adjustment to the response
Avoid diuretics because they conflict with hospice symptom goals
Start metolazone before trying a loop diuretic for congestion
Use spironolactone as a more potent diuretic than furosemide
explanation:
Loop diuretics relieve fluid overload and can serve a comfort goal in advanced heart failure. **Try furosemide for painful edema and adjust to response and tolerance**.

**A. Monitored furosemide.** Follow edema, comfort, blood pressure, renal function and electrolytes as appropriate.
**B. Avoid diuretics in hospice.** Medicines that relieve distress can be entirely consistent with hospice.
**C. Metolazone first.** It is generally an adjunct for inadequate response to loop therapy.
**D. Spironolactone more potent.** It does not provide the same robust diuresis as a loop diuretic and can raise potassium in CKD.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1181, 1182.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A woman with advanced illness requests a survival estimate to plan her affairs. When a clinical estimate is available, how does Hazzard recommend communicating it?
o: Provide a precise date and narrow the discussion of possible outcomes
Provide a range and acknowledge uncertainty in the estimate
Emphasize an optimistic point estimate when describing expected survival
Provide a numerical estimate and set aside the emotional response
explanation:
Communicating prognosis should support planning and allow an emotional response. **Offer a range and acknowledge uncertainty** when an estimate is available and desired.

**A. Give a precise date.** Individual survival varies even with similar disease severity.
**B. Range with uncertainty.** Describe the likely course and what could make it shorter or longer.
**C. Optimistic point estimate.** It may distort decisions and omit plausible less favorable outcomes.
**D. Ignore emotion.** Understanding and emotional support matter as much as the number.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 84-year-old woman with colon cancer is three days after hemicolectomy. She pulls out her Foley catheter and becomes agitated when staff try to replace it. CAM findings include acute onset, inattention, and disorganized thinking. She takes donepezil 10 mg for mild dementia; electrolytes are normal and hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL. Review confirms no ongoing indication for the catheter. Which step addresses this source of immobilization?
o: Replace the catheter and add wrist restraints during care
Retain catheter use while increasing the donepezil dose
Leave out the catheter and monitor a voiding trial
Retain catheter use while starting intramuscular haloperidol
explanation:
A bladder catheter can immobilize a patient and become a focus of distress. A medically unnecessary catheter offers no benefit that balances these risks.
**Leave the catheter out and monitor whether she voids adequately.**

**A. Replace the catheter and add wrist restraints during care.** Replacing the tether and adding restraints combines two recognized precipitants.
**B. Retain catheter use while increasing the donepezil dose.** Increasing donepezil does not relieve the discomfort or restriction from the catheter.
**C. Leave out the catheter and monitor a voiding trial.** A monitored voiding trial permits mobility and identifies retention if it develops.
**D. Retain catheter use while starting intramuscular haloperidol.** Haloperidol suppresses behavior without addressing an unnecessary device.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 882, 887–888, Table 58-5

q: An 86-year-old woman with truncal herpes zoster presents 48 hours after rash onset. She is immunocompetent, creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min, and there is no ocular involvement. Which virus-directed treatment is appropriate to reduce acute pain and the duration of chronic pain according to Hazzard?
o: Oral gabapentin adjusted according to tolerability
Oral valacyclovir for a full seven-day course
Topical acyclovir applied over the affected skin
Oral prednisone followed by a gradual dose taper
explanation:
Systemic antiviral treatment started early in shingles reduces acute pain and can shorten persistent pain. She presents at 48 hours with localized truncal disease and a creatinine clearance of 65 mL/min. **Give valacyclovir 1 g orally three times daily for seven days.**

**A. Oral gabapentin.** It can relieve neuropathic pain when analgesia is inadequate. It has no antiviral activity.
**B. Oral valacyclovir.** Her rash began within the 72-hour treatment window studied, and her renal function permits the usual zoster regimen.
**C. Topical acyclovir.** Applying antiviral cream to the vesicles provides no meaningful benefit for shingles.
**D. Oral prednisone.** Occasionally used alongside an antiviral for severe acute pain, prednisone alone does not treat zoster or prevent postherpetic neuralgia.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1727–1728. Valacyclovir prescribing information, Table 1.
ref: Hazzard Ch 107 — OTHER VIRUSES: HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS INFECTION AND HERPES ZOSTER
chapterTitle: Other Viruses: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection and Herpes Zoster

q: ישנן הגדרות שונות לסרקופניה הכוללות שילוב של מדדים שונים. מהו שילוב הממצאים שמגדירים סרקופניה?
o: מבחן SIX MINUTE WALK פחות מ- 400 מ' + ירידה ב- HAND GRIP
מבחן St. Thomas risk assessment tool חיובי
ירידה ב- HAND GRIP + ירידה ב- LEAN BODY MASS
מבחן TIMED UP AND GO מעל 30 שניות + ירידה ב- LEAN BODY MASS
explanation:
Definitions of sarcopenia differ. **Under EWGSOP2, low handgrip strength plus low muscle quantity, such as low appendicular lean mass, confirms sarcopenia.** Reduced strength by itself indicates probable sarcopenia, while poor physical performance helps determine severity.

**A. Short six-minute walk and weak grip.** These show impaired endurance and strength but do not confirm reduced muscle quantity or quality.
**B. Positive St. Thomas fall-risk screen.** This identifies fall risk and does not directly measure muscle strength or mass.
**C. Weak grip and low lean mass.** Standardized grip testing measures strength. An appropriate body-composition measurement can confirm reduced muscle quantity.
**D. TUG over 30 seconds and low lean mass.** A prolonged TUG indicates poor performance, which has several causes. In EWGSOP2 it is a severity measure and does not replace the strength criterion.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 732–735. EWGSOP consensus 2010, PMID 20392703. EWGSOP2, 2019, doi:10.1093/ageing/afy169.
Key note: The earlier EWGSOP framework permitted low mass plus low physical performance or low strength. The grip-and-lean-mass answer directly satisfies the revised EWGSOP2 definition.

explanationSource.status: Sentence-level source-image corrections; original IMA 7e bibliography retained. Review notes identify unresolved passages.

q: לפי חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, איזה מסמך מאפשר לאדם לקבוע מראש מי יקבל עבורו החלטות רפואיות כאשר יאבד כשירות בעתיד?
o: צוואה המסדירה את חלוקת הרכוש והנכסים לאחר מותו של האדם
ייפוי כוח מתמשך (Durable Power of Attorney)
טופס DNR המבטא מראש בקשה שלא לבצע החייאה בעת דום לב
הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות לפי החוק הנפרד לחולה הנוטה למות
explanation:
אדם המסוגל להבין את העניין רשאי לבחור מראש מי ייצג אותו בהחלטות רפואיות לאחר שיתקיימו תנאי הכניסה לתוקף. **ייפוי כוח מתמשך (Durable Power of Attorney)**.

**א. צוואה המסדירה את חלוקת הרכוש והנכסים לאחר מותו של האדם.** צוואה עוסקת בעיקר ברכוש לאחר המוות ואינה מינוי רפואי בחיים.
**ב. ייפוי כוח מתמשך (Durable Power of Attorney).** ייפוי כוח מתמשך יכול להקנות סמכות בענייני בריאות בהתאם להיקפו.
**ג. טופס DNR המבטא מראש בקשה שלא לבצע החייאה בעת דום לב.** הוראת אי־החייאה עוסקת בהתערבות מסוימת ואינה ממנה נציג כללי.
**ד. הנחיות רפואיות מקדימות לפי החוק הנפרד לחולה הנוטה למות.** הנחיות לפי חוק החולה הנוטה למות עוסקות בתנאי תחולה ובטיפולים מוגדרים.

אסמכתא · משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך, עמ׳ 4, 10, 12.
ref: משרד המשפטים, מדריך לממנה בייפוי כוח מתמשך
label: Source: מדריך לממנה - ייפוי כוח מתמשך · PDF pp4,10,12

q: מה המשפט המתאר את הסיכון לשברים בחוליות בחולים עם אוסטאופורוזיס?
o: שבר קודם בגולגולת, אך לא בעצמות האף, מהווה גורם סיכון לשבר נוסף
צפיפות עצם אינה מנבאת את הסיכון לשבר בחוליה בגברים
שבר קודם בחוליה מהווה גורם סיכון לשבר נוסף
עודף משקל מעלה את הסיכון לשבר בחוליה
explanation:
A low-trauma vertebral fracture is evidence of skeletal fragility and a powerful marker of future fracture risk. **A previous vertebral fracture predicts further fractures**, even if it was discovered incidentally.

**A. Skull but not nasal fracture.** Skull and facial fractures are generally traumatic and are not typical osteoporotic sentinel fractures.
**B. BMD cannot predict in men.** Bone density contributes to risk estimation in men as well as in women, though it is only one component.
**C. Previous vertebral fracture.** The risk of another vertebral or other fragility fracture rises after an initial vertebral fracture.
**D. Overweight increases vertebral risk uniformly.** Low body weight is a recognized general risk factor. Excess weight has a more complex relationship with site-specific fracture risk.

Reference · LeBoff et al., The Clinician's Guide to Prevention and Treatment of Osteoporosis, 2022, doi:10.1007/s00198-021-05900-y. Hazzard 8e, p. 769.

q: בת 92, מאושפזת במחלקה נוירולוגית לאחר אירוע מוחי עם פלגיה מלאה מימין. מה מהבאים מהווה קונטראינדיקציה להפנותה לאשפוז שיקומי?
o: חוסר שיתוף פעולה בטיפול
הפרעות בליעה המצריכות הזנה בזונדה
פצע לחץ דרגה 4 בעקב ימין
אפזיה מוטורית
explanation:
שיקום פעיל לאחר שבץ דורש יכולת להשתתף בטיפול ולהפיק תועלת מתרגול חוזר. מעריכים זאת בפועל בעזרת הנחיות קצרות, הדגמה ותקשורת מותאמת.

**חוסר יכולת לשתף פעולה במידה המאפשרת תרגול מונע בשלב זה הפניה לאשפוז שיקומי פעיל. אם הסיבה הפיכה, מטפלים בה ומעריכים מחדש.**

**A. חוסר שיתוף פעולה בטיפול.** כאשר גם בהכוונה מתאימה אי אפשר לבצע תרגול בעל מטרה, קשה להפיק תועלת מהמסגרת השיקומית.
**B. דיספגיה והזנה בזונדה.** ניתן לתת תמיכה תזונתית במקביל לשיקום. בודקים אם מצבה הרפואי מאפשר השתתפות בטוחה.
**C. פצע לחץ בדרגה 4 בעקב.** הפצע דורש טיפול והפחתת לחץ. אם אפשר להתאים את התרגול, דרגת הפצע לבדה אינה שוללת קבלה.
**D. אפזיה מוטורית.** קושי בהפקת דיבור אינו בהכרח קושי בהבנת הוראה. אפשר להיעזר במחוות, בהדגמה ובקלינאות תקשורת.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, חוזר מינהל רפואה 4/2009, סעיפים 5.2–5.3, עמ׳ 4.
ref: אמות מידה למתן טיפול שיקומי לקשישים

q: על פי מחקר ה- Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) בארה"ב, איזה מהבאים נכון בנוגע לדרכים למניעת סוכרת בגיל המבוגר?
o: ישנה יעילות שווה ל- METFORMIN ולשינוי אורחות חיים בהשוואה לפלצבו
שינוי אורחות חיים יעיל יותר בהשוואה לשימוש ב- METFORMIN
טיפול ב- METFORMIN יעיל יותר בהשוואה לשינוי באורחות החיים
טיפול ב- METFORMIN יעיל יותר במבוגרים לעומת צעירים
explanation:
The Diabetes Prevention Program compared intensive lifestyle intervention and metformin in people at high risk of type 2 diabetes. Activity combined with dietary change improved glucose handling with modest weight reduction.

**Lifestyle intervention was more effective than metformin in older participants.** During three years of active treatment, progression fell by more than 70% versus control among those over 60.

**A. Equal efficacy.** The effects diverged particularly clearly in the older age group.
**B. Lifestyle more effective.** The largest reduction in progression among older participants followed the structured lifestyle intervention.
**C. Metformin more effective.** Metformin had a smaller effect than lifestyle in this age group.
**D. Metformin works better in older participants.** Metformin was more effective in younger participants. The age advantage favored lifestyle intervention in older adults.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1565–1566, Figure 99-6.

q: לאיזה מהבאים יש קורלציה גבוהה עם TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY?
o: ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE
NORMAL PRESSURE HYDROCEPHALUS
AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS
MENINGIOMA
explanation:
Traumatic brain injury may precede persistent cognitive decline or hydrocephalus. **Secondary posttraumatic hydrocephalus can resemble normal pressure hydrocephalus. The association with later dementia is clearer than a specific link to Alzheimer pathology**.

**A. Alzheimer disease.** Dementia after injury has several potential causes and cannot be equated with Alzheimer disease.
**B. Normal pressure hydrocephalus.** Disrupted CSF circulation after trauma can produce gait, urinary and cognitive symptoms.
**C. ALS.** An early association may reflect falls during emerging motor disease. A sustained causal link is uncertain.
**D. Meningioma.** Reported observational associations do not demonstrate that trauma caused an individual tumor.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 997, and Yoon et al., Korean Journal of Neurotrauma 2018, pp. 86–92.
Key note: Both Alzheimer disease and normal pressure hydrocephalus received credit. Hazzard describes cohort and autopsy studies finding no specific association with an Alzheimer diagnosis or pathology.
chapterTitle: TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY AND CHRONIC TRAUMATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY
keySource: IMA 2024-May Subspecialty official answer key after appeals, Q63

q: A 76-year-old man is assessed after a fragility fracture of the wrist. He has diabetes, smokes, and sometimes falls. Which principle should guide assessment of his risk of another fracture?
o: Prioritize bone density while giving less weight to his fall history
Integrate prior fracture with assessment of falls and sarcopenia
Prioritize body weight while giving less weight to his prior fracture
Prioritize glycemic control while giving less weight to fall-related factors
explanation:
Fractures occur when the force of a fall exceeds bone strength. **Integrate the previous fragility fracture with falls, sarcopenia and bone assessment** to estimate this man's future fracture risk.

**A. Bone density over fall history.** Density describes skeletal susceptibility, while falls determine exposure to impact.
**B. Integrate fracture, falls and sarcopenia.** The prior fracture is independently prognostic. Muscle weakness and falls can add modifiable risks.
**C. Weight over prior fracture.** Body weight is relevant but cannot replace the strong risk signal from the wrist fracture.
**D. Glycemic control over fall factors.** Diabetes merits treatment, yet it does not remove the need to assess balance, strength and falls.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 769–770.

q: איזה מהשינויים הפיזיולוגיים הבאים מאפיין את מערכת הלב וכלי הדם בזקנה?
o: קיצור של PR ו- QRS
התפתחות של היצרות מסתמים
עליה בקשיחות (Stifness) של חדר שמאל וירידה בהרפיה דיאסטולית
הרחבת עורקים וירידה בהיענות (impedence) של האאורטה
explanation:
Diastolic filling depends on the left ventricle relaxing and stretching. With normal aging, **left ventricular stiffness increases and diastolic relaxation slows**, so early filling is less efficient.

**A. Shorter PR and QRS intervals.** Conduction can slow with aging. Shortening reverses the expected direction.
**B. Valvular stenosis.** Degenerative valve changes become common, but hemodynamically significant narrowing is disease rather than an inevitable physiologic change.
**C. Stiffer ventricle, slower relaxation.** Both changes impair ventricular filling and can occur without overt cardiac disease.
**D. Arterial dilation with lower aortic compliance (called impedance in the option).** The aorta can dilate and become less compliant with age, so the Hebrew wording is plausible. Impedance describes opposition to pulsatile flow and increases as the aorta stiffens. Calling the two terms equivalent reverses the impedance finding.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1116, 1121, Tables 73-1 and 73-2.
Key note: Hazzard describes aortic dilation, arterial stiffening and increased aortic impedance. The Hebrew part of the fourth option describes reduced compliance, which fits stiffening, but its English parenthesis incorrectly equates compliance with impedance.

q: What hip-flexion angle should be avoided after posterolateral-approach total hip arthroplasty during early recovery?
o: More than 90 degrees
No limitation on hip flexion
Only less than 90 degrees
Only 120 to 150 degrees
explanation:
During early recovery after a traditional posterolateral hip replacement, deep hip flexion can increase the risk of dislocation. A raised chair or toilet seat allows sitting with less bend at the hip.

**When posterior precautions are prescribed, avoid flexing the hip beyond 90 degrees during early recovery.**

**A. More than 90 degrees.** This is the usual flexion boundary in the traditional posterior precautions. A low seat can bring the hip beyond it.
**B. No limit on flexion.** Deep bending may put the healing joint at risk when a flexion precaution has been prescribed.
**C. Only less than 90 degrees.** This reverses the direction of the restriction. The concern is excessive flexion.
**D. Only 120 to 150 degrees.** Waiting until this range would permit flexion beyond the 90-degree boundary. Hip precautions apply before those angles are reached.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 832.

q:
בת 74, התקבלה למיון עם חולשה לאחר מחלת חום. בבדיקת גזים בדם בחדר המיון הממצאים הבאים:
מדד ויחידות מידה | ערך לחולה | ערכי הנורמה
PH | 7.56 | 7.37-7.44
PCO2 mmHg | 38 | 40-51
HCO3 mmol/L | 33 | 22-26
Na mEq/L | 140 | 135-145
Cl mEq/L | 91 | 96-106
K mM/L | 4 | 3.5-5
איזו חולה מתאימה להפרעת חומצה בסיס זו?
o: חולה סוכרתי עם טיפול ב- METFORMIN מאושפז בטיפול נמרץ
חולה עם צירוזיס לא מפוצה, ומיימת שמקבל אלדקטון.
חולה עם COPD ואי ספיקת לב, שמקבל טיפול במשתנים.
חולה עם דלקת ריאות שהונשם עקב בצקת ריאות
keySource: IMA 2026-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q139
explanation:
Elevated bicarbonate indicates metabolic alkalosis, but PCO₂ has not risen as expected for compensation. **Combined metabolic and respiratory alkalosis** is the pattern. Among the vignettes, cirrhosis with diuretic exposure is the closest clinical example.

**A. Critically ill metformin-treated patient.** Metformin-related lactic acidosis would lower bicarbonate. Critical illness can produce mixed disorders but does not specify this pattern.
**B. Cirrhosis with ascites on spironolactone.** Cirrhosis can promote hyperventilation, while a separate chloride-depleting process can raise bicarbonate. Spironolactone itself is not the classic cause of contraction alkalosis.
**C. COPD and heart failure with diuretic use.** COPD with CO₂ retention and diuretic use commonly gives respiratory acidosis plus metabolic alkalosis, with elevated PCO₂.
**D. Ventilated patient with pneumonia and pulmonary edema.** Ventilator settings and lung disease can alter PCO₂, but the diagnoses alone do not explain the high bicarbonate and relative hypocapnia.

Reference · Harrison 22e, Table 58-2, pp. 367–368.
Key note: All four vignettes received credit. Harrison's example with these values is combined metabolic and respiratory alkalosis in end-stage liver disease with ascites and diuretic use.
